newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU likely to relaunch grain exports - officials.
newsitem.headline: EU likely to relaunch grain exports - officials.

text.p: The European Union is likely to decide on Thursday to resume its stalled grain export mechanism for soft wheat, barley and rye, member country officials said on Tuesday.

The EU's cereals management committee has export tenders for the three grain types on its agenda for a possible vote at weekly talks in Brussels, and officials said the panel of 15 countries was likely to bow to industry requests to open the tenders and allow exports to resume.

The EU suspended virtually all wheat exports in April, followed soon afterwards by other grains, to help keep domestic prices down amid uncertainty over this year's crop. But the long-awaited decision to resume exports -- while not guaranteeing actual sales -- would give a boost to a grain market anxious to secure business for the next campaign.

"It is obviously a signal," said one member country official, adding domestic prices were now fairly low. The EU seems to be heading for another large grain crop of around 200 million tonnes but recent rain has increased fears over the quality of some wheat and barley.
No maximum volume was available for the planned tenders, at which traders will bid for subsidies for exports from the free market. But officials said the volume would not be a big issue.

If the EU panel adopts the tenders on Thursday, the earliest date at which they could officially start is July 17, the next time the cereals committee meets. The panel, which normally meets each Thursday, is due to meet every two weeks in July and August. The Commission has said it would take two to three weeks to open the tenders once a vote had been taken. --Tim Hepher, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
